logic_node.action: Titrate antihypertensive medications to blood pressure targets
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HFpEF and hypertension should have medication titrated to attain blood pressure targets in accordance with published clinical practice guidelines to prevent morbidity. RAAS antagonists including ACEi, ARB, MRA, and possibly ARNi could be first-line agents.

source_text: Patients with HFpEF and hypertension should have medication titrated to attain blood pressure targets in accordance with published clinical practice guidelines to prevent morbidity.

logic_node.action: Consider SGLT2i to reduce HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFpEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality. EMPEROR-Preserved showed empagliflozin reduced primary composite endpoint by 21% with 29% reduction in HF hospitalization. Benefit was similar irrespective of diabetes status.

source_text: In patients with HFpEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality.

logic_node.action: Manage atrial fibrillation to improve symptoms
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFpEF, management of AF can be useful to improve symptoms. Individualize strategies for rate or rhythm control. Beta blockers and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are often considered first-line for heart rate control.

source_text: In patients with HFpEF, management of AF can be useful to improve symptoms.

logic_node.action_detail: In selected patients with HFpEF, MRAs (e.g., spironolactone) may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of the spectrum. TOPCAT showed HF hospitalization reduction (HR 0.83). Post hoc criteria: LVEF >=45%, elevated BNP or HF admission within 1 year, eGFR >30, creatinine <2.5 mg/dL, potassium <5.0 mEq/L.

source_text: In selected patients with HFpEF, MRAs may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum.

logic_node.action_detail: In selected patients with HFpEF, the use of ARB (e.g., candesartan) may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of the spectrum. CHARM-Preserved showed nonsignificant trend toward benefit (HR 0.89) with lower HF hospitalizations in the candesartan arm.

source_text: In selected patients with HFpEF, the use of ARB may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum.

logic_node.action_detail: In selected patients with HFpEF, ARNi (sacubitril/valsartan) may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of the spectrum. PARAGON-HF showed benefit signal for HF hospitalizations (rate ratio 0.85) and greater benefit in patients with LVEF 45%-57% and in women.

source_text: In selected patients with HFpEF, ARNi may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum.

logic_node.action: Avoid routine use of nitrates or PDE5 inhibitors
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFpEF, routine use of nitrates or phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors to increase activity or quality of life is ineffective. NEAT-HFpEF showed no beneficial effects of isosorbide mononitrate on activity levels, QOL, or exercise tolerance. RELAX trial showed sildenafil did not improve oxygen consumption or exercise tolerance.

source_text: In patients with HFpEF, routine use of nitrates or phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors to increase activity or QOL is ineffective.

logic_node.action: Monitor potassium and renal function on MRA therapy
logic_node.action_detail: When using spironolactone in HFpEF, careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing at initiation and follow-up are key to minimizing risk of hyperkalemia and worsening renal function. Eligibility criteria from TOPCAT: eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73 m2, creatinine <2.5 mg/dL, and potassium <5.0 mEq/L.

source_text: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing at initiation and follow-up are key to minimizing the risk of hyperkalemia and worsening renal function.

logic_node.action_detail: HFpEF is defined as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF >= 50%). HFpEF is highly prevalent, accounting for up to 50% of all patients with HF, and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. It is a heterogeneous disorder contributed to by hypertension, diabetes, obesity, CAD, CKD, and specific causes such as cardiac amyloidosis.

source_text: HFpEF (LVEF >= 50%) is highly prevalent, accounting for up to 50% of all patients with HF, and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality.
